_evidence_note: TEST / PREVIEW FIXTURES — NOT REAL INVENTORY.
The House of Assets connector was not authorized in the session that built
this, so no live PUBLIC_SITE export could be read. These records exist to
prove the engine end to end: ingestion, identity ownership, the specialized
renderer, the detail route, the governed price state and the governed CTA.
`evidence` is TEST_PREVIEW and the runtime renders a visible preview notice
on every page while it stays that way. Replace this file (or point
window.SF_FEED_URL at a live export) and set evidence to LIVE; nothing in
Two of these records are REAL, already-shipped Sentinel Fortune work and are
marked real_artefact: Floor and S.5 ASCENT Lite. The rest are fixtures and
The last four records are deliberately INVALID. They are the governance
evidence: each must be refused, and platform/tests asserts exactly why.

records.title: Origin Echo
records.summary: A generative pad built in the browser — not a recording.
records.description: Four detuned voices layered into an unresolved chord. Nothing is streamed and nothing was recorded: the browser synthesises it live each time you press play. It exists as a demonstration of the listening room, not as a release.

records.title: The Quiet Wire
records.summary: Test fixture — the opening entry of a storyworld that has not been written.
records.description: A placeholder narrative record used to prove the story renderer, the series collection surface and the detail route. No episode, script or film exists behind it.

records.title: S.5 ASCENT Lite
records.summary: A side-on precision platformer. Hand-built levels, keyboard or touch.
records.description: Move, jump, collect, climb. A real playable game: a 42 KB engine reading hand-authored level data. Free, no account, nothing to install. Your best score stays in your own browser.

records.title: Floor
records.summary: Know the price below which a job loses you money.
records.description: Enter your annual overhead, billable hours, labour cost and target margin. Floor works out what every billable hour has to contribute before anything is profit, then gives each job a break-even price floor and the price that would have hit your target margin. Runs in your browser; nothing is uploaded. It is arithmetic on figures you enter, not accounting, tax or financial advice.

metadata.audience: Owner-operators of small trades and home-service businesses
metadata.evidence: 39 unit tests and 15 end-to-end checks passing

records.title: The four questions that make an estimate defensible
records.summary: Estimates lose money in what they leave out.
records.description: Test fixture pointing at real published writing. Four questions, asked before the estimate goes out, close most of the gap between what you quoted and what the job cost.

records.title: Stillness, first
records.summary: Test fixture — a reflective passage that has not been written.
records.description: A placeholder record used to prove the reading room: one passage, one column, no onward call to action. Reflective writing, not therapy and not medical or psychological advice.

records.title: Ledger Watch
records.summary: Test fixture — a workflow diagnostic that has not been built.
records.description: A placeholder technical record used to prove the workshop renderer and its contract strip. It declares a job, its inputs and its outputs because a system that cannot be described that way does not belong in the workshop.

metadata.takes: A month of job records as CSV
metadata.returns: Which workflow step is losing hours

records.title: Operations Starter
records.summary: Test fixture bundle — two systems, one price.
records.description: A placeholder bundle used to prove bundle membership resolution and the commerce renderer. Nothing is for sale.

records.title: First Collection
records.summary: Test fixture — a curated collection with no published products behind it.
records.description: A placeholder commercial record used to prove the lookbook renderer and the Digital Shop handoff. The production catalogue holds no published products, so nothing here is for sale.
records._why_invalid_cta: Deliberate: a BUY with no governed price. The commercial heart must DISABLE this button and say the price is not published — never render a buy button with no price.

records.title: Unapproved Release
records._why_invalid: publicationStatus is DRAFT. House of Assets never routed it to the public site.

records.title: Truthy Approval
records._why_invalid: approved is the string "yes", not boolean true. A string is not a decision — the shop publication bridge refuses this too.

records.title: Unknown Identity
records._why_invalid: identity is not one of the seven. Refused, never defaulted into a house that does not own it.

records.title: Local Link
records.summary: Public, but its CTA must be stripped.
records.description: This record is itself public and valid. Its CTA points at a localhost address, which must never reach a public link however it got into the feed. The record renders; the button does not.
records._why_partially_invalid: The destination host is not on the allow-list. governedDestination refuses it, normalizeCta drops the whole CTA, and the commercial heart renders 'Not yet available.' instead of a dead button.

records.title: Withdrawn Title
records._why_invalid: withheld is true. Something pulled it back after approval, and a withdrawal must win over an earlier approval.
